Apple was ruled to have infringed a Masimo patent covering the low-power blood oxygen detection feature on the Apple Watch, nearly a year ago.

Apple was ordered at the time to pay US$634 million in damages, but a federal judge recently ordered Apple to pay an additional US$184 million in interest...

Apple's dispute with medical technology company Masimo is being fought on multiple fronts simultaneously. One of the more serious ones was a 2023 ruling by the International Trade Commission requiring them to remove the blood oxygen feature from two Apple Watch models before they could be sold in the United States. Apple in Cupertino was forced to redesign how the feature operates before being allowed to bring the product into the US market.

Apple is also facing another lawsuit from Masimo seeking damages for using its low-power blood oxygen measurement patented technology. Apple was ultimately found to have infringed the patent and was ordered to pay what should have been paid as patent licensing fees as damages.

According to Bloomberg Law, Apple has now been ordered to pay an additional US$184 million in interest on that amount.

There is also good news for Apple. Masimo had requested interest calculated at 7%, but the judge refused, ruling that the interest rate should be equivalent to the rate Masimo itself pays on its borrowings. However, even calculated at annual compound interest, this still adds US$184 million to the amount owed.
